title: Darwin Godel Machine — Open-Ended Self-Modifying Agents

questions.question: What is the key difference between true_score and reported_score in this simulator?
options: reported_score can add hack_bonus when the evaluator side channel is open, while true_score counts exact cases
true_score is produced by the agent and reported_score is always lower
true_score ignores the tool output and reported_score runs the tests
They are aliases for the same floating-point value
questions.explanation: true_score is the external exact-case score; reported_score adds the agent's hack bonus only when hack_allowed is enabled, capped at 1.0.

questions.question: If an agent adds hack_bonus but the side channel is closed, what happens to true_score?
options: It is increased by the bonus
It remains the exact fraction of cases transformed correctly
It is replaced by the archive key
It becomes zero after every mutation
questions.explanation: The bonus affects only reported_score under hack_allowed; true_score is recomputed from the actual transformed cases.

questions.question: Which fields make two candidates occupy different archive cells?
options: Only the random seed
Only whether the candidate was generated in round 200
The number of operations and rounded reported score
The target string and the quiz stage
questions.explanation: run_dgm keys its archive by (len(ops), round(reported_score, 2)), so both program length and reported fitness affect the cell.

questions.question: Why can no tool-only sequence in the default TOOLS list reach a perfect score on all CASES?
options: The evaluator never runs the sequence
The trim tool always deletes the answer
Every input contains an unknown operation
The target includes title-case behavior, but title is not one of the available tools
questions.explanation: The cases require collapse, trim, and title-case; the manifest has the first two but no title operation, so the true score has a ceiling below 1.0.

questions.question: What observable warning distinguishes the open side-channel run from the closed run?
options: reported_score can exceed the corresponding true_score
The target cases disappear
All candidates receive exactly zero
The evaluator starts changing the tool list
questions.explanation: With --reward-hack-allowed, reported_score includes a bonus that is not present in true_score, exposing the evaluator mismatch.

questions.question: What does apply do when a candidate contains an unknown operation name?
options: It treats the operation as title-case
It returns an empty string
It skips the operation and reports a perfect score
It adds the name to TOOLS
questions.explanation: The implementation checks the tool lookup and returns an empty string for an unknown operation rather than extending the manifest.
